Container.Name: kemlock-server
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted password vault server for Kemlock, Amethystora Vault and Bitwarden apps. One small static binary, SQLite by default, post-quantum key exchange and OPAQUE sign-in. Reads Vaultwarden's settings, so a Vaultwarden data folder can be mounted as /data to migrate.
First start: there is no admin token. The server prints a one-time setup code in its log (click the container, then Logs); its setup page asks for that code before it makes the first admin account.
Put it behind a reverse proxy with TLS (Nginx Proxy Manager, SWAG, Caddy or Traefik) and set Domain to the public address: DPoP proofs are checked against it. WebSocket routes are /notifications/hub and /kem/v1/live.

Config.Name: Web port
Config.Description: The API, the web vault and both WebSocket routes, on one port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The database, server.key, attachments and backups. Back up server.key apart from the data.

Config.Name: Domain
Config.Description: The public address clients use, such as https://vault.example.com. Required behind a proxy.

Config.Name: Allow sign-ups
Config.Description: Let anyone who can reach the server make an account. Off after the first admin exists.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: error, warn, info, debug or trace.

Config.Name: Client IP header
Config.Description: Behind a proxy, the header that carries the client address, such as X-Forwarded-For.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Comma-separated proxy addresses the client IP header is trusted from, such as your proxy container's IP.

Config.Name: Database URL
Config.Description: Empty uses SQLite in /data. Or postgres://user:password@host/kemlock.
